[enumerateCommands(root)](./sh-analysis.enumeratecommands.md)

</td><td>

Observes represented command invocations (`CallExpr`<!-- -->) reachable from `root`<!-- -->, with its resolved words ([resolveWord()](./sh-analysis.resolveword.md)<!-- -->) and the path used to reach it ([CommandContext](./sh-analysis.commandcontext.md)<!-- -->). Descends everywhere a command can occur: statement lists, both sides of `&&`<!-- -->/`||`<!-- -->/pipelines, subshells/blocks, if/case branches \*and\* conditions, loop bodies \*and\* conditions, function bodies, background/negated/coproc statements, and — critically — `CmdSubst`<!-- -->/`ProcSubst` nested inside words, wherever those words occur (arguments, redirection targets, case subjects/patterns, loop word lists, assignment values, test/arithmetic operands, …), not only inside `CallExpr.Args`<!-- -->.

An assignment-only `CallExpr` (`FOO=bar`<!-- -->, `args` empty) has no first word to resolve and is not itself a command invocation — no program runs — so it produces no [CommandSite](./sh-analysis.commandsite.md)<!-- -->; any command substitution nested in its assigned value (`FOO=$(sub)`<!-- -->) is still found and reported.

`commands` are sorted by source position (`nodePos(node).Offset`<!-- -->), so nested command substitutions and out-of-structural-order redirection targets still come back in source order regardless of traversal order.

Facts only, matching [resolveWord()](./sh-analysis.resolveword.md)<!-- -->'s posture: no safety verdict, no command/wrapper allowlist or denylist, no dataflow. A statically unknown `argv0` (`static: false`<!-- -->) is a normal, expected result.

A long \*linear\* chain — `|`<!-- -->/`|&`<!-- -->/`&&`<!-- -->/`||` of any realistic length — is traversed iteratively and never risks a stack overflow or trips the nesting-depth guard below, regardless of how many stages/links it has.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[resolveArgv0(site, options)](./sh-analysis.resolveargv0.md)

</td><td>

Follows `site`<!-- -->'s argv0 through zero or more \*transparent wrappers\* — commands modeled as locating and re-executing another command (`env FOO=1 rm -rf /`<!-- -->, `command rm`<!-- -->, `nohup rm`<!-- -->, `sudo -u x "$prog"`<!-- -->) — to the \*\*effective\*\* command word under those configured assumptions. This is not runtime lookup or a complete inventory of programs embedded in arguments.

The wrapper table ([ResolveArgv0Options.transparentWrappers](./sh-analysis.resolveargv0options.transparentwrappers.md)<!-- -->, defaulting to [DEFAULT\_TRANSPARENT\_WRAPPERS](./sh-analysis.default_transparent_wrappers.md)<!-- -->) is plain data: each [WrapperSpec](./sh-analysis.wrapperspec.md) declares how to locate the word it wraps, and neither this function nor the table encodes any safety judgment about \*which\* commands are dangerous — matching [CommandSite](./sh-analysis.commandsite.md)<!-- -->'s and [resolveWord()](./sh-analysis.resolveword.md)<!-- -->'s "facts only" posture. A caller can drop a default entry (that name then resolves as an ordinary, non-transparent command) or add their own (e.g. a project's `with-retry` helper) and both directions are followed identically to any built-in entry.

\*\*A statically-unknowable word is never guessed through\*\* — four distinct cases all stop the chain immediately at that word rather than falling back to any other guess:

1. `argv0` or any wrapper's located word itself resolves `static: false` (an expansion, tilde, glob, …) — `sudo -u x "$prog"` reports `effective: { static: false, reason: 'expansion' }` with `chain: [<sudo>, <"$prog">]`<!-- -->, not `rm`<!-- -->/`sudo`<!-- -->/anything static. 2. A \*statically known\* word shaped like a flag (`-`<!-- -->-prefixed, not `--`<!-- -->) doesn't match any flag/operand shape the current [WrapperSpec](./sh-analysis.wrapperspec.md) recognizes — `sudo -D /tmp rm x` (`-D` isn't modeled for `sudo`<!-- -->) reports an `effective` of `static: false` with `reason: 'unknown-flag'`<!-- -->. An unmodeled flag cannot identify a wrapped command or justify skipping its possible operands. 3. A recognized flag's value structurally embeds the real command rather than naming it as a separate word — `env -S 'rm -rf /'` reports `effective: { static: false, reason: 'embedded-command' }` (see [WrapperSpec.unresolvableFlags](./sh-analysis.wrapperspec.unresolvableflags.md)<!-- -->'s doc comment).

2. The effective command is a shell interpreter ([DEFAULT\_EMBEDDED\_COMMAND\_INTERPRETERS](./sh-analysis.default_embedded_command_interpreters.md)<!-- -->) invoked with `-c` — `bash -c "$x"`<!-- -->, `sudo sh -ec ls` — and the command that runs is inside the string operand. The result is the same `'embedded-command'` shape `env -S` produces: the interpreter word is `chain.at(-2)` and `chainIndices.at(-1)` is the option word that selected `-c`<!-- -->. `bash script.sh`<!-- -->, `bash -e script.sh`<!-- -->, `bash -- -c` and `bash -o c` are not `-c` invocations and resolve to `bash` as before. A dynamic word in option position (`bash "$f" -c x`<!-- -->, `bash -c"$y" x`<!-- -->) is undecidable, so the interpreter stays a static `bash`<!-- -->: `static: true` then means only that the name is known, not that the command is a plain shell invocation. The `-c` string itself is never parsed.

Known limits: the table models common option spellings, not a full emulation of each shell's option parser. Unusual spellings can be misclassified in either direction:

- Bash/sh single-dash long options after a short option, e.g. `bash -e -rcfile M`<!-- -->. - `ksh -c +c M`<!-- -->, or a dynamic word after `-c` that expands to an option. - mksh's selector-bearing operands in `mksh -o -c M` and `mksh -o +c M`<!-- -->. - A lone `+` before `-c`<!-- -->, e.g. `bash + -c M`<!-- -->. - Zsh grammar switches, e.g. `zsh -o shoptionletters -b -c M`<!-- -->.

`VAR=val` shell-assignment prefixes on the `CallExpr` itself (`CommandSite.node.Assigns`<!-- -->, e.g. `FOO=bar rm x`<!-- -->) are always skipped and counted in [Argv0Resolution.assignmentsSkipped](./sh-analysis.argv0resolution.assignmentsskipped.md) — a mechanism distinct from a wrapper's own `VAR=val` \*operands\* (`env A=1 rm x`<!-- -->, `sudo A=1 rm x`<!-- -->), which [WrapperSpec.assignmentOperands](./sh-analysis.wrapperspec.assignmentoperands.md) handles per-wrapper.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[resolveWord(word, options)](./sh-analysis.resolveword.md)

</td><td>

Determines whether a `Word` node is statically a known string, and if so, what that string is — the atom of shell-AST static analysis (e.g. "is this word literally `rm`<!-- -->"). A word is static iff every part is a literal after shell unquoting: a bare `Lit` (backslash escapes processed), a `SglQuoted` (including `$'...'` ANSI-C escapes decoded), or a `DblQuoted` containing only literal parts (and not itself a `$"..."` locale translation) — including concatenations of these (`'r'm` resolves to `"rm"`<!-- -->). A word containing any expansion (`ParamExp`<!-- -->, `CmdSubst`<!-- -->, `ArithmExp`<!-- -->, `ProcSubst`<!-- -->), a triggering unquoted `~` (see `options.context`<!-- -->), an unquoted glob metacharacter/bracket expression/`ExtGlob`<!-- -->, potential brace expansion, a `$"..."` locale translation, or an unrepresentable ANSI-C escape has a nonstatic resolution, never a safety judgment (see [WordResolution](./sh-analysis.wordresolution.md)<!-- -->). Failure to complete an observation is separate: host-copy resource refusal and binding failures propagate explicitly rather than becoming a word-resolution result.

</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

<tr><td>

[EmbeddedCommandInterpreterSpec](./sh-analysis.embeddedcommandinterpreterspec.md)

</td><td>

A data-only description of one shell interpreter whose `-c` option makes the next operand a command string run by that shell (`bash -c 'rm x'`<!-- -->). Like `env -S`<!-- -->, the command that runs lives \*inside\* an operand, so [resolveArgv0()](./sh-analysis.resolveargv0.md) reports `'embedded-command'` instead of the interpreter's own name as the effective command. The selector `c` is reserved: exact-token fields (`noOperandLongOptions`<!-- -->, `operandLongOptions`<!-- -->, `optionTerminatorWords`<!-- -->) cannot contain `-c`<!-- -->.

Only the option grammar needed to decide \*whether `-c` is an option\* is described: which options consume an operand word (so that `-o c` or `-o pipefail -c` are not misread) and where option parsing ends. Everything else about the interpreter — what its other options mean, whether a given option name is valid — is irrelevant to that decision and unmodeled; an invalid invocation that a real shell would reject is still reported conservatively, since nothing is guessed about what it would run.

Option parsing ends at the first statically known word that is not an option, at `--`<!-- -->, at a lone `-`<!-- -->, or at a table-defined terminator; afterwards a word shaped like `-c` is an ordinary script operand. A dynamic word in option position leaves the question undecidable, so scanning stops and the interpreter is reported exactly as before (its own static name). In that case `static: true` means only that the interpreter's name is known; it does not mean the command is a plain shell invocation, because `bash "$f" -c x` runs `x` when `$f` is `-x`<!-- -->.

This shape may grow new optional fields in a \*\*minor\*\* release; existing fields' meaning never changes.

</td></tr>

[WrapperSpec](./sh-analysis.wrapperspec.md)

</td><td>

A data-only description of one "transparent wrapper" — a command whose own argv0 is modeled as locating and re-executing another command (`env`<!-- -->, `sudo`<!-- -->, `nohup`<!-- -->, …). [resolveArgv0()](./sh-analysis.resolveargv0.md) interprets every field here structurally (skip N words, recognize this literal flag, …); adding a new `WrapperSpec` never requires a code change to [resolveArgv0()](./sh-analysis.resolveargv0.md) itself — that's what makes [DEFAULT\_TRANSPARENT\_WRAPPERS](./sh-analysis.default_transparent_wrappers.md) data rather than a set of hardcoded `if (name === 'env')` branches, and what lets a caller extend or replace the table with their own project-specific wrappers (e.g. a `with-retry` helper).

Every flag/operand-recognizing field is checked against a word's \*statically resolved\* text only (its `.text` on a [WordResolution](./sh-analysis.wordresolution.md) `static: true` result) — a dynamic word can never be identified as one of a wrapper's own flags or operands (see [resolveArgv0()](./sh-analysis.resolveargv0.md)<!-- -->'s doc comment for why an unrecognizable word always ends the chain rather than being guessed through).

This shape may grow new optional fields in a \*\*minor\*\* release as this analyzer models more wrapper flag conventions; existing fields' meaning never changes.

</td></tr>

<tbody><tr><td>

[DEFAULT\_EMBEDDED\_COMMAND\_INTERPRETERS](./sh-analysis.default_embedded_command_interpreters.md)

</td><td>

`sh-analysis`<!-- -->'s default [EmbeddedCommandInterpreterSpec](./sh-analysis.embeddedcommandinterpreterspec.md) table: the shells whose `-c` option makes [resolveArgv0()](./sh-analysis.resolveargv0.md) report `'embedded-command'`<!-- -->. Each entry's option grammar is hand-derived from the cited manual. Basic clusters and required operands were cross-checked on Linux bash 5.2.21, dash 0.5.12, zsh 5.9, ksh93u+m 1.0.8 and mksh R59. Long-option, termination and omitted-operand cases were checked on macOS bash 5.3.9 and 3.2.57 (also `/bin/sh`<!-- -->), Apple dash-16, zsh 5.9 and ksh93u+ AJM 2012-08-01. Omitted `-o`<!-- -->/`+o` operands before another signed option were confirmed only on that ksh93u+ build, not ksh93u+m or mksh. Builds can differ: macOS's ksh93u+ differs from the cited 93u+m for `ksh -o c "echo X"`<!-- -->. The `sh` entry also models bash's long options because `sh` can be bash. Named options that change the option grammar itself (such as zsh's `shoptionletters`<!-- -->) are not interpreted; a custom table is needed for that grammar. It is data, not policy: it names no dangerous commands and a caller can replace or extend it via [ResolveArgv0Options.embeddedCommandInterpreters](./sh-analysis.resolveargv0options.embeddedcommandinterpreters.md)<!-- -->; an empty array restores the behavior in which an interpreter is an ordinary effective command.

Frozen, including each entry and its arrays.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[DEFAULT\_TRANSPARENT\_WRAPPERS](./sh-analysis.default_transparent_wrappers.md)

</td><td>

`sh-analysis`<!-- -->'s default [WrapperSpec](./sh-analysis.wrapperspec.md) table — every entry's flag/operand handling is hand-derived from that wrapper's own manual page (or, for shell builtins, the Bash Reference Manual/POSIX Shell &amp; Utilities volume), cited per entry below, and cross-checked empirically against the real utility where one was locally available (GNU coreutils `env`<!-- -->/`nice` directly; `sudo` via `sudo -h`<!-- -->'s usage/option summary only — never executed, per this package's "facts only" posture and basic safety hygiene). This table is \*data\*, not policy: it names no "dangerous" commands, makes no safety judgment, and a caller can freely replace or extend it via [ResolveArgv0Options.transparentWrappers](./sh-analysis.resolveargv0options.transparentwrappers.md) under the same explicit grammar contract.

Frozen (including each entry object and its own array/regexp fields) so immutability of this shared, module-scoped table is a contract, not just a convention any importer happens to honor. Per-call wrapper options are separate values and cannot mutate these shared defaults.

`xargs` is deliberately \*\*excluded\*\*: unlike every entry here, `xargs` doesn't simply re-exec a single wrapped command word it can point to statically — it invokes `command [initial-arguments]` once per \*batch\* of additional arguments assembled from its own stdin at run time (batched per `-n`<!-- -->/`-L`<!-- -->/line-splitting rules, GNU xargs(1)). Treating it as transparent would misrepresent what's actually invoked: the "wrapped command" is only ever a syntactic \*prefix\* of the real, stdin-dependent argv, and that prefix can itself be entirely absent (bare `xargs` reruns each stdin-derived line as its own command). No `WrapperSpec` shape here can honestly express that, so `xargs` is left for a caller to model explicitly if their use case calls for it, rather than shipped as a silently-wrong default.

</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

[Argv0UnresolvedReason](./sh-analysis.argv0unresolvedreason.md)

</td><td>

Why [resolveArgv0()](./sh-analysis.resolveargv0.md) couldn't identify a single, definite effective command — distinct from [WordResolutionReason](./sh-analysis.wordresolutionreason.md)<!-- -->, which is about why one \*word\*'s text is unknowable at the shell-syntax level (an expansion, a glob, …). `Argv0UnresolvedReason` instead reflects `resolveArgv0`<!-- -->'s own wrapper-table-driven analysis of an otherwise statically-known word:

- `'unknown-flag'` — a statically known word shaped like a flag (starts with `-`<!-- -->, isn't exactly `--`<!-- -->) for the wrapper currently being followed, but that doesn't match any flag/operand shape [WrapperSpec](./sh-analysis.wrapperspec.md) recognizes for it. Never guessed through as the wrapped command — see [resolveArgv0()](./sh-analysis.resolveargv0.md)<!-- -->'s doc comment. - `'embedded-command'` — a wrapper flag whose value structurally embeds the real command rather than naming it as a separate word (e.g. `env -S 'rm -rf /'` — see [WrapperSpec.unresolvableFlags](./sh-analysis.wrapperspec.unresolvableflags.md)<!-- -->'s doc comment), or a shell interpreter's `-c` option (`bash -c 'rm x'`<!-- -->, see [EmbeddedCommandInterpreterSpec](./sh-analysis.embeddedcommandinterpreterspec.md)<!-- -->). In both cases the chain's second-to-last element is the wrapper or interpreter word, so its name stays available. - `'ambiguous-assignment'` — a statically known assignment operand whose acceptance differs across supported utility implementations, such as `env =value cmd` (GNU/glibc accepts an empty name; BSD rejects it). Neither the following command nor the operand itself is guessed as the effective command.

This union may grow in a \*\*minor\*\* release (mirroring `WordResolutionReason`<!-- -->'s and `CommandContext`<!-- -->'s semver policy in `resolve-word.ts`<!-- -->/`enumerate-commands.ts`<!-- -->) — a reason this version doesn't yet know about only ever accompanies `static: false`<!-- -->; an exhaustive `switch` should still include a `default` case.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[CommandContext](./sh-analysis.commandcontext.md)

</td><td>

A single frame of the path from the root of the tree down to a [CommandSite](./sh-analysis.commandsite.md)<!-- -->, describing \*how\* the command is reached — never whether it is safe to run. `CommandSite.context` is an ordered stack of these, outermost frame first:

- `'and'`<!-- -->/`'or'` (`side: 'right'`<!-- -->) — the right-hand operand of a `BinaryCmd` (mvdan/sh's node for both `&&` and `||`<!-- -->); only the right side is tagged; the left side inherits the surrounding context unchanged, since it runs unconditionally relative to this operator. - `'pipeline'` (`stage: n`<!-- -->) — one stage of a `|`<!-- -->/`|&` chain (also a `BinaryCmd`<!-- -->, left-associatively nested by mvdan/sh); every stage is tagged, 0-indexed left to right, regardless of whether the chain mixes `|` and `|&`<!-- -->. - `'subshell'` — inside a `Subshell` (`( ... )`<!-- -->). - `'cmdSubst'`<!-- -->/`'procSubst'` — inside a `CmdSubst` (`$(...)`<!-- -->/backticks) or `ProcSubst` (`<(...)`<!-- -->/`>(...)`<!-- -->) reached from \*any\* word-bearing position (an argument, a redirection target, a case subject, a loop's word list, an assignment value, a test/arithmetic operand, …) — not only from `CallExpr.Args`<!-- -->. - `'if'` (`branch: 'cond' | 'then' | 'else'`<!-- -->) — inside an `IfClause`<!-- -->'s condition, then-branch, or else-branch (mvdan/sh nests `elif` chains as `IfClause.Else` pointing to another `IfClause`<!-- -->, so an `elif`<!-- -->'s own condition/then are reached through an `{kind:'if',branch:'else'}` frame first, then their own `'cond'`<!-- -->/`'then'` frame — reflecting the real nesting rather than collapsing it). - `'case'` — inside one `CaseClause` branch's statement list (not the case subject word or the patterns). - `'loop'` (`role` is `'body'` or `'cond'`<!-- -->) — inside a `ForClause`<!-- -->'s statement list (`role: 'body'` only — a `for` loop has no statement-list condition) or a `WhileClause`<!-- -->'s (`role: 'cond'` for the condition, `role: 'body'` for the loop body). - `'function'` (`name`<!-- -->) — inside a `FuncDecl`<!-- -->'s body; `name` is the function's literal name text. - `'background'`<!-- -->/`'negated'` — the enclosing `Stmt` has mvdan/sh's Background/Negated flag set (`cmd &`<!-- -->, `! cmd`<!-- -->). - `'coproc'` — inside a `CoprocClause`<!-- -->'s statement (a `coproc` block, optionally named).

A `Block` grouping (`{ ...; }`<!-- -->) and a `TimeClause` (`time cmd`<!-- -->) are deliberately transparent — grouping and timing a command doesn't change how it's reached, so no frame is added for either.

This union may grow in a \*\*minor\*\* release — a future mvdan/sh grammar construct this module starts modeling can add a new `kind` variant without that being a breaking change (mirroring [WordResolutionReason](./sh-analysis.wordresolutionreason.md)<!-- -->'s semver policy in `resolve-word.ts`<!-- -->). It is deliberately not sealed against extension elsewhere in the codebase. Every existing variant's shape (its extra fields, if any) is stable — only new variants are ever added — so an exhaustive compile-time `switch` over `.kind` should still include a `default` case to stay forward-compatible.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[WordResolution](./sh-analysis.wordresolution.md)

</td><td>

The result of statically resolving a `Word` node's text. Reports facts only — never a safety verdict, never a hardcoded command/wrapper list. `static: false` ("unknowable") is a first-class, valid result, not an error condition.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[WordResolutionReason](./sh-analysis.wordresolutionreason.md)

</td><td>

Why a [resolveWord()](./sh-analysis.resolveword.md) result is `static: false`<!-- -->: the word's exact value cannot be classified as one reliably known literal word.

- `'expansion'` — the word contains a `ParamExp` (`$x`<!-- -->, `${x}`<!-- -->), a `CmdSubst` (command substitution, either `$(...)` or backtick form), an `ArithmExp` (`$((expr))`<!-- -->), or a `ProcSubst` (`<(cmd)`<!-- -->/`>(cmd)`<!-- -->) part: its value depends on program state (variables, command output, process substitution) that only exists at run time. - `'tilde'` — an unquoted, unescaped `~` triggers Bash tilde expansion (Bash Reference Manual §3.5.2, "Tilde Expansion") at the start of the word, or — when `resolveWord`<!-- -->'s `context` option is `'assignment-value'` or omitted — immediately after an unquoted `:` anywhere in the word too (§3.5.2 also documents this for assignment-statement values, e.g. `PATH=/foo:~/bar`<!-- -->). Either way: statically shaped, but its value depends on the filesystem/environment (`$HOME`<!-- -->, NSS user database lookups) at run time. See `resolveWord`<!-- -->'s `context` parameter doc for the full command-argument-vs-assignment-value distinction. - `'glob'` — the word contains an unquoted, unescaped glob metacharacter (`*`<!-- -->/`?`<!-- -->), an unquoted bracket expression (`[...]` — an unquoted `[` with a later unquoted `]` in the same word, POSIX 2.13.1 / Bash Reference Manual §3.5.8.1, "Pattern Matching"), or an `ExtGlob` part (Bash Reference Manual §3.5.8, "Filename Expansion"): its value depends on which filesystem entries exist at run time. - `'brace'` — the word contains a `BraceExp` part or the pinned upstream `syntax.SplitBraces` produces one on a private observation copy (Bash Reference Manual §3.5.1, "Brace Expansion"). Parser output is unchanged. This reports potential expansion in supporting dialects; a bare Word has no dialect or shell-option state, so even POSIX-parsed words receive the conservative classification. It does not claim POSIX sh expands braces. - `'locale'` — the word contains a `$"..."` locale-translated string (Bash Reference Manual §3.1.2.5, "Locale-Specific Translation"): its value is looked up in the current locale's translation catalog at run time via `gettext`<!-- -->, regardless of whether its contents also contain an expansion. `'locale'` takes precedence over any `'expansion'` a `$"..."` word's \*contents\* would otherwise report — the `DblQuoted` node's own `dollar` flag is checked before its children are visited at all, so e.g. `$"hi $x"` reports `'locale'`<!-- -->, never `'expansion'`<!-- -->. - `'unsupported'` — the input cannot support an exact Unicode-text claim: an escape crosses caller-constructed word-part boundaries; a brace candidate has escape handling this analyzer cannot trust; a word contains nil/typed nil parts or byte-valued strings; or ANSI-C quoting produces NUL, non-ASCII byte escapes, or non-scalar Unicode escapes (U+D800..U+DFFF or values above U+10FFFF, such as `$'\\uD800'` and `$'\\UFFFFFFFF'`<!-- -->). Shell bytes must not be replaced with invented Latin-1 or replacement text. Supported scalar Unicode decoding assumes a UTF-8 shell locale; byte-string and arbitrary locale decoding are outside this text observation.

Reason descriptions do not establish universal precedence among features. Whole-word `unsupported` preflight takes precedence even when a caller has already supplied a `BraceExp`<!-- -->: an escape crossing parts can invalidate the apparent quoting boundaries, and an escape-uncertain brace candidate remains uncertain. Independently quoted or fully protected literal siblings do not suppress a known `BraceExp`<!-- -->. After preflight, existing resolution order can select a triggering tilde or earlier glob before visiting that part.

This union may grow in a \*\*minor\*\* release — new mvdan/sh word-part node types, or new statically-shaped-but-dynamic categories, can add new reason strings without that being a breaking change. It is deliberately not sealed against extension elsewhere in the codebase. A reason string this version of the package doesn't yet know about only ever accompanies `static: false`<!-- -->, never changes the meaning of `static: true`<!-- -->, so runtime consumers that only branch on `.static` are safe by construction across such additions; an exhaustive compile-time `switch` over `.reason` should still include a `default` case to stay forward-compatible.

</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
